--- title: "Syllable deletion (all positions)" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_SUPRESION_SILABAS_TP" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_SUPRESION_SILABAS_TP`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Supresión de sílabas (todas las posiciones)*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_SUPRESION_SILABAS_TP.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Syllable deletion (all positions), from age 7 to 8 (1,940 administrations in 3 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .40. AUC .69–.71 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1941 | | Battery | DIS-ESP | | Format | auditory stimuli | | Items | 14 (1941) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child was instructed to delete a speech sound and to provide the remaining word or pseudoword. Correct responses, errors and time were recorded. The child deletes the initial. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:--------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1941|Supresión de sílabas |Estímulos pregrabados con cascos | 14| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 7, 8| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1941.** Pseudopalabras pregrabadas (el niño no ve la pantalla, con cascos); 3 ejemplos orales previos. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1941 · Supresión de sílabas](../../figuras/plataforma/1941.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1941"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/CF523.html) and [rapid naming](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/RAN.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 7.1| 2010| 184|2017/18 | 804| 256| 547| 31| | 7.1| 2012| 899|2019/20 | 214| 210| 0| 14| | 8.1| 2011| 900|2019/20 | 419| 0| 419| 25| | 8.2| 2010| 639|2018/19 | 503| 143| 360| 25| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|----------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 7.1| 466| 2010, 2012| 9.11| 3.76| 10| -0.74| 3.86| 9.66| | 8.2| 143| 2010| 10.62| 3.06| 11| -1.23| 1.40| 16.08| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–14 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 7.1| 466|0–14 |0–14 |0–14 | | | 8.2| 143|0.4–14 |0–14 |0–14 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .40 (median .40, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .82. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 7.1| 8.2| 458| 0.46| 0.40| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .57–.63. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Verbal memory (7.1, r = .41); Verbal memory (8.1, r = .42); Verbal memory (8.2, r = .46). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .69–.71. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .50–.60. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABAS_TP_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .60–.76 (3 time points; 225–311 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 7.1| 466| 2010, 2012| 1.2| 3.5| 5| 7| 10| 12| 13| | 8.1| 419| 2011| 4.9| 6.0| 7| 9| 11| 13| 14| | 8.2| 143| 2010| 5.0| 6.2| 8| 9| 11| 13| 14| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_SILABAS_TP_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 7.1| 972| 0.013| 0.694| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 1,018| 0.067| 0.287| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 1,017| 0.007| 0.820| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 1,018| 0.076| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.1| 418| 0.245| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.1| 419| -0.005| 0.963| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.1| 418| -0.053| 0.276| |School (ICC) | 8.1| 419| 0.133| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.2| 503| 0.145| 0.001| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.2| 492| 0.061| 0.503| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.2| 491| -0.090| 0.046| |School (ICC) | 8.2| 503| 0.079| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Syllable deletion (all positions)” (code 1941; DIS-ESP battery) assesses syllable awareness (deletion). Stimuli are presented auditorily and the child responds by selecting on the screen. It comprises 14 items. The time limit is 240 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 4 sessions, from 7 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .82 (N = 1,554, 14 items). Stability across time points was ρ = .40. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .50–.60. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 8.2 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
